primary.poolable_reason: THE POOL STANDS, AND EVERY STEP OF IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. THE ESTIMAND IS THE SAME IN ALL THREE REGISTRATIONS. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ANCOVA and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE STRINGS IS 'Percent' AGAINST 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. ALL THREE PER-TRIAL VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN, DIGIT FOR DIGIT: ORION-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). ALL THREE ARM PAIRS SUM TO THEIR REGISTRATION'S RECORDED ENROLMENT EXACTLY: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. ARM LABELS AND ROLES ARE CORRECT ON ALL THREE. AND THE POOLED VALUE REPRODUCES: DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. THE CARD, THE OBJECT AND THE INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION ALL AGREE.

effect_measure: all three are ANCOVA mean differences in percent change in LDL-C, read from each trial's own registry results record

heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: Higgins I-squared = (Q - df) / Q, clamped at 0. Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.2.
heterogeneity.i2_definition_evidence: Decided by recomputing BOTH definitions from this object's own per-trial inputs: Higgins gives 71.9988 and REML/metafor gives 71.9988 against the stored 71.9988.

primary.heterogeneity_status: Q = 7.1426 on 2 df, I-squared 72.0 per cent, tau-squared 9.52 under DerSimonian-Laird and 10.60 under REML. HIGH, AND ON ONLY THREE STUDIES. The Hartung-Knapp interval is -63.71 to -44.30.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, plus a comparison of between-study variance estimators
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.10.4.4: methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better, and restricted maximum likelihood is the RevMan default. Section 10.14 governs the leave-one-out half. Cited to 10.10.4.4 rather than 10.10.4.5 because 10.10.4.5 is about INTERPRETATION with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval, not the variance estimator -- a miscitation this repository has already made once and corrected.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Two decisions. First, whether the pooled reduction depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the between-study variance estimator and interval method -- which at k=3, with the house rule against DerSimonian-Laird below k=10, is not a formality but the reason this table exists.
sensitivity.conclusion: NO SINGLE TRIAL CARRIES THIS RESULT. Omitting each in turn gives -55.56 (-59.62 to -51.50), -52.18 (-55.85 to -48.51) and -53.90 (-61.84 to -45.97). All three exclude no effect and the pooled point moves by at most 1.8 percentage points on a scale of 54.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Three between-study-variance estimators, each with Wald and Hartung-Knapp intervals. This pool is published under DerSimonian-Laird at k=3, and this project's own rule is REML or Paule-Mandel below k=10, so the first question a reader should be able to answer is whether that choice made the answer.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: IT DID NOT. The point estimate spans -53.95 to -54.00 across all six combinations -- a range of five hundredths on a scale of fifty-four -- and every one of the six intervals excludes no effect, the widest by more than forty percentage points. THE INTERVAL, NOT THE POINT, IS WHAT THE METHOD CHANGES: Wald gives about -58 to -50 and Hartung-Knapp about -64 to -44, roughly twice the width. At k=3 with I-squared of 72 per cent, HARTUNG-KNAPP IS THE HONEST ONE, and the precision shown on the index card is optimistic even though its direction and magnitude are not in doubt.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: The published DerSimonian-Laird value is RETAINED as the headline. It reproduces exactly, and moving a correct published number by five hundredths of a percentage point would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question for the whole corpus, not a finding about this topic, and it is parked as such.

pooled.stands_because: THE POOL STANDS, AND EVERY STEP OF IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. THE ESTIMAND IS THE SAME IN ALL THREE REGISTRATIONS. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ANCOVA and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE STRINGS IS 'Percent' AGAINST 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. ALL THREE PER-TRIAL VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN, DIGIT FOR DIGIT: ORION-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). ALL THREE ARM PAIRS SUM TO THEIR REGISTRATION'S RECORDED ENROLMENT EXACTLY: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. ARM LABELS AND ROLES ARE CORRECT ON ALL THREE. AND THE POOLED VALUE REPRODUCES: DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. pooled.caveats: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW ANYWAY, NONE OF WHICH OVERTURNS THE ESTIMATE. (1) THE ESTIMATOR IS NOT THIS PROJECT'S OWN STANDARD FOR THIS k. DerSimonian-Laird underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or Paule-Mandel below k=10. This pool is k=3. IT WAS RECOMPUTED UNDER BOTH: Paule-Mandel gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. THE CHOICE OF ESTIMATOR DOES NOT CHANGE THIS ANSWER, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) HETEROGENEITY IS HIGH AND k IS SMALL: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- MUCH WIDER than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the PRECISION on the card is optimistic. (3) THE THREE POPULATIONS ARE NOT THE SAME: ORION-9 enrolled heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, ORION-10 atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, ORION-11 ASCVD or risk-equivalents. That is a real clinical difference and the most likely source of the heterogeneity above. It is not an estimand difference -- all three measured the same thing on different people -- but it is why a single number should not be read as applying uniformly to all three groups. (4) LDL-C PERCENT CHANGE IS A SURROGATE. This review pools a laboratory value, not an event. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, myocardial infarction or stroke, and no such claim should be read into it. (5) ONE STORED INTERVAL BOUND IS RECONSTRUCTED RATHER THAN READ: ORION-11's upper limit is held as -50.34 where the registry prints -50.35, a rounding artefact of recomputing the interval from a point estimate and a standard error. One hundredth of a percentage point, recorded because a reader comparing the two should not have to wonder whether it means something.
pooled.card_note: endpoint definitions read and CONFIRMED identical in all three registries, every value matches the registry; but I² 72% on k=3, so the Hartung-Knapp interval −63.7 to −44.3 is the honest one

primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.
